# Incident Report: NetSupport RAT Infection

## Victim Host
| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.11.26.183** |
| MAC address | **d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** (NetBIOS workstation name; also seen as domain member of `NEMOTODES`/`nemotoads.health`) |
| Logged-in domain user | **oboomwald** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ/AS-REP exchanges with DC `10.11.26.3`, realm `NEMOTODES.HEALTH`) |
| Domain Controller | 10.11.26.3 (NEMOTODE-DC / NEMOTODES-DC.nemotoads.health) |

## Malware Family
**NetSupport RAT** (malicious repurposing of the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-access client).

**Attribution: signature-confirmed**, corroborated by protocol-level evidence:
- Suricata/ET alerts explicitly name it: `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`, `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`, `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin/Response`, `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`.
- The HTTP `User-Agent` on every C2 request is literally `NetSupport Manager/1.3`.
- Extracted C2 request/response bodies use NetSupport's native client protocol tokens verbatim: `CMD=POLL`, `INFO=1`, `ACK=1`, and `CMD=ENCD` / `ES=1` / `DATA=<encrypted blob>` — this is the documented NetSupport client32.exe check-in/encrypted-data format, not a generic HTTP beacon.

## Timeline / Infection Chain (2024-11-26, UTC)
1. **04:49:38** – Host boots/reconnects; issues benign Microsoft NCSI check (`www.msftconnecttest.com`).
2. **04:50:00–04:50:16** – Browsing chain consistent with a fake-CAPTCHA/"ClickFix" lure:
   - `classicgrand.com` (213.246.109.5)
   - `confirmsubscription.com` (52.8.34.0, 13.56.30.207)
   - `css.createsend1.com` / `js.createsend1.com` (18.160.156.61/103, abused Campaign Monitor CDN)
   - `code.jquery.com`
3. **04:50:14** – DNS lookup and TLS session to **`modandcrackedapk.com`** (193.42.38.139) — flagged by Suricata as `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup` and `... in TLS SNI`. This is the payload-delivery domain for the RAT (session is TLS-encrypted, so the actual dropped file/binary could not be extracted from this capture).
4. **04:50:40** – Certificate revocation check to `r10.o.lencr.org` (OCSP), consistent with a freshly-run/installed binary validating a TLS cert.
5. **04:50:45** – RAT executes immediately:
   - Geolocation lookup: `GET /location/loca.asp` to **`geo.netsupportsoftware.com`** (104.26.1.231:80) → returned coordinates `33.7488,-84.3877`.
   - C2 check-in begins to **194.180.191.64:443** via `POST http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm`, `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`.
6. **04:50:45 → 05:43:29 (end of capture)** – Persistent beaconing to the same C2, roughly every 60 seconds (`CMD=POLL` keepalives interleaved with `CMD=ENCD` encrypted data exchanges), confirming an active, interactive RAT session for the remainder of the capture.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint (RAT check-in/control channel)**
- `194.180.191.64:443` — HTTP POST to `/fakeurl.htm`, `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`, ~60-second beacon interval, sustained for the entire capture.

**Supporting/staging infrastructure (malicious domains and resolved IPs)**
- `modandcrackedapk.com` → 193.42.38.139 (payload delivery site; ET-flagged as "ZPHP" domain)
- `classicgrand.com` → 213.246.109.5
- `confirmsubscription.com` → 52.8.34.0, 13.56.30.207
- `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` → 104.26.1.231 (NetSupport's own geolocation service, queried by the RAT client itself, not attacker-controlled — included as a RAT-behavior IOC)

**Malicious URLs observed**
- `https://modandcrackedapk.com/` (TLS SNI only, content encrypted)
- `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` (repeated C2 POSTs)
- `http://geo.netsupportsoftware.com/location/loca.asp`

**Transferred files / hashes**
- No plaintext executable or archive transfer was observed in this capture — the likely payload delivery occurred inside the encrypted TLS session to `modandcrackedapk.com`, so no file name or SHA256 hash could be recovered from the traffic.
- Only file-like objects extractable via HTTP were the RAT's own protocol artifacts (`fakeurl.htm` C2 responses, `loca.asp` geolocation reply) and unrelated legitimate traffic (Microsoft `connecttest.txt`, Adobe `ProcessMAU.txt`, Windows Update `.cab` files) — none are malicious payloads.

## Assessment
`oboomwald`'s workstation (DESKTOP-B8TQK49, 10.11.26.183) was compromised via a fake-CAPTCHA/verification lure chain ending at `modandcrackedapk.com`, which delivered NetSupport RAT. The RAT established persistent, encrypted C2 with `194.180.191.64:443` and remained beaconing for the full duration of the capture (~53 minutes), indicating an active attacker-controlled remote-access session on the host during the incident window.
